2. The facts relevant for the disposal of the Rule, in short, is that the land of Baratali Mouja under Mohongonj Upazila of Netrakona District being SA Khatian No. 577 in SA Plot No. 292/293 and BRS Khatian No.250 in BRS Plot No. 502/503 measuring 0.40 acres of land were recorded in the name of the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-6 and their predecessors while have been in possession thereof sold the same in favour of the plaintiff and his brother on 3-10-1970 and accordingly the plaintiffs have been owning and possessing 0.20 acres of land and that during BRS, record of right the aforesaid land has been wrongly recorded in the name of the predecessor of the defendants which are mistakenly held and correction of the same is necessary and hence the petitioner has filed Land Survey Tribunal Case No. 580 of 2014 under section 145A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. At the time of filing the Land Survey Tribunal Case on 29-1-2014, the petitioner furnished Court fee of Taka 300 and the same was accepted accordingly. The defendants appeared before the tribunal and they by filing a compromise petition on 30-3-2014 accepted the claim of the plaintiff and pursuant to a Solehnama both the parties adduced evidence on 15-9-2014. On 28-2-2016 the learned tribunal accepted the Solehnama, but passed an order to the effect that as per Article 12(ii) of the Schedule-II of the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as amended on 1-8-2008 and coming in to force on 1-9-2010 Court fee would be Taka 1,000, but the case has been filed with the Court fee of Taka 300 only and there remains outstanding Court fee of Taka 700 and directed the plaintiff to pay a remaining Court fee of Taka 700 within 21 (twenty one) working days, failing which the plaint shall stand rejected. The petitioner challenging this order has filed this writ petition and obtained Rule and order of stay. 

 "to alter or cancel any entry in a register of the names of proprietors of revenue paying estates, should have to be paid at the rate of Taka 1,000." 

 6. It is very clear that if anything has been recorded in the register and the plaintiff files any application or suit or case to alter or cancel the register, the Court fee should have to be paid of Taka 1,000 as per provision of Article 12(ii) of schedule II of the Court-Fees Act, 2010 (Amended). Now, the question is what is the meaning of "proprietor", "revenue paying estates" and the "register"? The legal definition of register is agenda, album, almanac, archive, arrangement, balance sheet, calendar, catalogue, chronicle, chronology, day book, diary, docket, ephemeris, file, journal, ledger, liber, list, loc, log book, minutes, notes, proceedings, record, registration book, roll, roster, schedule, tabulate, written record. The definition of proprietor has been defined in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 "Proprietor" means a person owning, whether in trust or for his own benefit, an estate or a part of an estate." 

 8. Now let us see what is the meaning of the estate? The meaning of 'estate' is given in definition clause 2(11) of the said Act which runs as follows: 

 "Estate" means land included under one entry in any of the general Registers of revenue-paying lands and revenue-free lands, prepared and maintained under the law for the time being in force by the Collector of a districts, and includes Government khas mahals and revenue-free lands not entered in any register." 

 10. From the above mentioned prayers and statements made in the plaint it is very clear that it was the case for correction of the record. What is record? We have already stated that the register means record. From the definition of register it is found that record means register. Since record is the register, as per said Article 12(ii) it is also clear that, to alter or cancel any entry in the register of the names of proprietors of revenue paying estates Court fees must be paid as per provision of Article 12(ii) of the Schedule 2 of the Court-Fees Act as amended in 2010. Since the petitioner is the proprietor of a particular estate and he has prayed for correction of the record which is a register. The learned judge of the Land Survey Tribunal, Netrakona has passed a very correct order to pay Court fee of Taka 1,000, which is legal and has been passed in accordance with law. There is nothing to interfere with this order.
